cards.front: What should you know about who definition?
cards.back: The World Health Organisation defines health as "a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity."

cards.front: Recall a key point about Health and Fitness
cards.back: Health is NOT just the absence of illness. A person can be free from disease but still have poor mental or social health. True health requires well-being in all three areas.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Health and Fitness
cards.back: Fitness is "the ability to meet the demands of the environment" or "the ability to meet the demands of a physical task." It refers to how well the body can cope with the physical challenges it faces.

cards.front: What should you know about key concept?
cards.back: Health and fitness are related but they are NOT the same thing. A person can be fit but not healthy, or healthy but not fit. Being fit can contribute to good health, but it does not guarantee it.

cards.front: What should you know about yes.?
cards.back: A person can be physically fit enough to perform a task even while having a health condition. For example, athletes with asthma (like runner Paula Radcliffe) can be extremely fit for their sport while managing a long-term health condition. However, ill health typically makes it harder to achieve and maintain fitness.

cards.front: What should you know about pe exam tips — health and fitness?
cards.back: 1. For Health and Fitness questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Health and Fitness to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

cards.front: What does Fit AND healthy mean?
cards.back: The person can meet the physical demands of their activity AND has complete physical, mental and social well-being (e.g. A recreational runner who trains regularly, eats well, has good social connections and positive mental health)

cards.front: What does Fit but NOT healthy mean?
cards.back: The person can meet physical demands but has health issues in one or more dimensions (e.g. An elite athlete with an eating disorder (mental health issue); a footballer playing through injury; an athlete with depression)

cards.front: What does Healthy but NOT fit mean?
cards.back: The person is free from disease and has good well-being, but cannot meet the physical demands of specific tasks (e.g. A person who is disease-free and happy but leads a sedentary lifestyle and cannot run for a bus without becoming breathless)

cards.front: What does Neither fit nor healthy mean?
cards.back: The person has health problems and cannot meet physical demands (e.g. A person with chronic disease who is physically inactive and socially isolated)

Students often think fitness and health are the same thing. Wrong: Fitness and health are the same thing Correct: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being (WHO). Fitness is the ability to meet the demands of the environment. You can be fit but unhealthy (e.g. a marathon runner with flu).
6 marks: Explain how health and fitness affects sporting performance.
